<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Fiscal 2010 compared with 2009</FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Revenues</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;Staffing Services revenues increased to $1.1 billion in 2010 from $954.1 million in the prior year.&nbsp; The increase was primarily due to increasing business volumes among existing customers in the United States and Canada as the economy continued to improve.</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: -0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0in 71pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face=Symbol>&#183;</FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 7pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">By skill&#151;Light industrial revenues increased 27.2% from prior year levels due to higher volumes among several of our customers, primarily in the distribution, consumer products, and retail industries.&nbsp; Consistent with trends in past economic cycles, light industrial staffing tends to begin growing before other skills, including clerical. Clerical revenues increased 3.3% in 2010 compared with the prior year primarily due to several clients increasing their staffing needs due to the improvement in the economy.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: -0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0in 53pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: -0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0in 71pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face=Symbol>&#183;</FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 7pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">By service&#151;Temporary staffing revenues increased 12.9% compared with the prior year due to the improvement in the U.S. economy and as customers increased demand for light industrial temporary labor.&nbsp; Permanent placement revenues increased 20.1% in 2010 compared with the prior year primarily due to employers increasing their hiring to meet demands after significant reductions in their workforces. This revenue increase reflects slightly improving employment trends in the United States and Canada.</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: -0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0in 53pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Gross Profit</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;Gross profit increased to $171.1 million in 2010 compared with $149.3 million in the same prior year period.&nbsp; The overall gross margin was 15.9% in 2010 compared with 15.6% in the prior year.&nbsp; The increase of 30 basis points was due to a shift in our services due to an increase in permanent placement revenues (10 basis points) and higher temporary staffing margins (20 basis points) due to higher pay/bill spreads and lower employee burden costs.</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Segment Operating Profit (Loss)</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;Staffing Services segment operating profit was $18.2 million or 1.7% of revenues in 2010 compared with an operating loss of $0.7 million or (0.1%) in the prior year.&nbsp; Operating expenses increased by $2.9 million or 2.0% year over year, but decreased as a percentage of gross profit to 89.4% compared with 100.4% in the prior year.&nbsp; The decrease in operating expenses as a percentage of gross profit was primarily due to productivity improvements and continued effective management of our cost structure.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><FONT size=2>25</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
</DIV>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Outlook</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151; We continue to focus on executing our strategy of diversifying our customer base and expanding business with our targeted small and mid-sized accounts to obtain higher gross profit margins.&nbsp; Sales activity and improving operating leverage remain our major areas of focus for the upcoming year.&nbsp; Due to the sensitivity of our Staffing Services business to economic conditions, we continue to carefully monitor gross profit trends and expenses to achieve appropriate profitability.</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Fiscal 2009 compared with 2008</FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Revenues</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;Staffing Services revenues decreased to $954.1 million in 2009 from $1.2 billion in the prior year.&nbsp; Revenues decreased 21.8% from the prior year primarily due to lower business volumes among existing customers in the U.S. and Canada due to the slow economy.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: -0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0in 71pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face=Symbol>&#183;</FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 7pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">By skill&#151;Clerical revenues decreased 20.7% from prior year levels due to lower demand among various customers, primarily in the financial, business services and transportation industries.&nbsp; Light industrial revenues decreased 23.3% from prior year levels due to lower business volumes among several of our customers, primarily in the technology, consumer products, manufacturing and retail industries, and the loss of a large customer in mid-2008 due to unacceptable pricing.&nbsp; <BR>
<BR>
</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: -0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0in 71pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face=Symbol>&#183;</FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 7pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">By service&#151;Temporary staffing revenues decreased 21.4% compared with the prior year due to the slowing economy, which resulted in lower temporary employment in the U.S.&nbsp; Permanent placement revenues decreased 54.0% in 2009 compared with the prior year primarily due to employers significantly reducing their hiring in 2009 due to the weak economy in the U.S. and Canada.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: -0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0in 53pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Gross Profit</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;Gross profit decreased to $149.3 million or 15.6% of revenue in 2009 compared with $205.8 million or 16.9% in the prior year period.&nbsp; The decrease of 130 basis points in gross profit margin resulted from lower temporary staffing margins of 90 basis points due to lower pay/bill spreads (80 basis points) and higher payroll taxes and other employee burden costs (10 basis points) combined with a change in revenue mix resulting from disproportionally lower permanent placement revenues (40 basis points).</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></I></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Segment Operating (Loss) Profit</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;Staffing Services segment operating loss was $0.7 million compared with profit of $4.1 million in the prior year.&nbsp; Operating expenses as a percentage of gross profit increased to 100.4% compared with 98.0% in the prior year.&nbsp; Higher operating expenses as a percentage of gross profit were due to deleveraging as volumes and gross profit margins decreased faster than operating expenses were reduced.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Unallocated Corporate Costs</FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; 2010 compared with 2009</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;Unallocated corporate costs were consistent from year to year at $12.9 million or 0.6% of revenue in 2010 compared with $12.4&nbsp;million or 0.7% in 2009.</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; 2009 compared with 2008</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;Unallocated corporate costs decreased to $12.4 million in 2009 from $16.7 million in 2008, due to cost containment actions as business volumes decreased.&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">Unallocated corporate costs as a percentage of revenues were 0.7% and 0.8% in 2009 and 2008, respectively.</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><FONT size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><FONT size=2>26</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Liquidity and Capital Resources</FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></I><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Cash Flows</FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">As of December 26, 2010, we had total cash of $18.5&nbsp;million (an increase of $10.4 million from December 27, 2009).&nbsp; Total debt was $5.0 million as of December 26, 2010 compared with $13.6 million as of December 27, 2009.&nbsp; Cash flows from operating, investing and financing activities, as reflected in the accompanying Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, are summarized as follows (in thousands):</FONT></P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.35in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Operating cash flows</FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.35in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Cash provided by operating activities for 2010 was $63.3 million.&nbsp; Cash flow from operating activities before changes in working capital was $61.9 million, which increased from $32.8 million in 2009 due to higher adjusted earnings from continuing operations combined with low levels of cash taxes paid due to the utilization of existing deferred tax assets.&nbsp; Lower working capital employed contributed $1.4 million to operating cash flow in 2010 compared with&nbsp;$8.3 million in 2009.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.35in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Cash provided by operating activities for 2009 was $41.1 million.&nbsp; Cash flow from operating activities before changes in working capital was $32.8 million, which decreased from $48.6 million in 2008 due to lower adjusted earnings from continuing operations as the slower economy negatively impacted our operating results.&nbsp; Lower working capital contributed $8.3 million to operating cash flow in 2009.&nbsp; Cash generated from lower working capital resulted primarily from a decrease in accounts receivable compared with prior year-end levels due to lower revenue volume and improved DSO of 41 days at the end of 2009.&nbsp; This was partially offset by $10.9 million used for severance and leases related to restructuring and other charges (included in &#147;Accounts payable and accrued liabilities&#148; in the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows).</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.35in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Cash provided by operating activities for 2008 was $79.2 million.&nbsp; Cash flow from operating activities before changes in working capital was $48.6 million, which decreased from $74.6 million in 2007 due to lower earnings as the slower U.S. economy negatively impacted our financial results.&nbsp; Better utilization of working capital allowed us to generate $30.6 million of additional cash flow.&nbsp; Working capital decreased due to lower accounts receivable from improved DSO and lower revenues toward the end of 2008, partially offset by corresponding decreases in accrued salaries and wages, accounts payable and other liabilities.</FONT></P>

<A name="page_31"></A>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Investing cash flows</FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Cash used for investing activities of $34.3 million in 2010 primarily relates to the payment of $29.2 million, net of cash acquired, for the Tatum acquisition in the first quarter of 2010, $1.5 million of additional consideration paid in connection with a 2007 acquisition (i.e. an earnout payment) and capital expenditures of $4.6 million.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Cash used for investing activities of $4.3 million in 2009 was primarily due to the payment of $3.0 million related to a 2007 acquisition and the purchase of a franchised operation in 2009 and capital expenditures of $2.1 million, primarily related to the implementation of an upgraded telecommunications system.</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 24pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Cash provided by investing activities of $4.5 million for 2008 was primarily due to the return of $18.4 million of cash collateral from our restricted insurance deposit accounts upon the issuance of additional letters of credit as replacement collateral.&nbsp; This was partially offset by the payment of the final settlement of $5.3 million of indemnity claims related to the 2004 sale of the Australian education business and capital expenditures of $8.9 million which primarily related to computer hardware upgrades for acquired companies and new systems development.</FONT><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></B><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Financing cash flows</FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 35pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Cash used in f</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">inancing activities for 2010 of $18.6 million was primarily related to the repayments on our lines of credit of $10.7 million, repayment of other debt of $4.3 million and $4.2 million for the purchase of treasury shares.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 35pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Cash used in f</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">inancing activities for 2009 of $36.3 million was primarily related to the repayments on our lines of credit of $23.4 million, repayment of other debt of $4.4 million and $8.6 million for the purchase of treasury shares.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Cash used in f</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">inancing activities for 2008 of $90.8 million was primarily related to the repayments on our lines of credit of $49.9 million, repayment of other debt of $15.6 million, including the early payment of the Technisource deferred purchase price, and $25.3 million for the purchase of treasury shares.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Financing</FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We believe that a combination of our existing cash balances, other liquid assets, operating cash flows and existing revolving lines of credit, taken together, provide adequate resources to fund ongoing operating requirements.&nbsp; However, our operating cash flow could be impacted by factors outside of our control. </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">On October 29, 2010, the Company and its lenders entered into an amendment (the &#147;First Amendment&#148;) to the Amended and Restated Loan and Security Agreement (the &#147;Agreement&#148;), extending the maturity date of its U.S. dollar revolving line of credit (the &#147;Revolver&#148;) to November 15, 2014 and reducing the interest rate margins and fees.&nbsp; The First Amendment did not materially change any of the covenants contained in the Revolver.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; As of December 26, 2010, there was $0.05 million outstanding under this facility, and as of December 27, 2009, there was $10.8 million outstanding.&nbsp; As of December 26, 2010, total availability was $157.6&nbsp;million (calculated as eligible receivables of $224.2 million, less: borrowings outstanding of $0.05 million, letters of credit of $31.9 million and a one week payroll reserve of $34.6&nbsp;million).&nbsp; The interest rate on this line of credit is based upon the duration of the loan, availability under the line and other conditions and was approximately 4.75% (prime rate plus 1.50% margin) as of December 26, 2010.&nbsp; Pursuant to the terms of the Agreement, we pay an unused line fee in the range of 0.375% to 0.5% per annum that is determined by the unused portion of the revolving line of credit.&nbsp; For letters of credit, we pay an annual rate based on availability under the line (currently 2.5%) plus a fixed fronting fee of 0.125%.&nbsp; For further discussion on letters of credit, see Note 11, &#147;Commitments and Contingencies.&#148;</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The Revolver contains certain affirmative and negative covenants, the most significant of which is a minimum fixed charge coverage requirement under certain conditions.&nbsp; If excess availability, as defined by the Agreement, falls below $30.0 million, we are required to maintain a fixed charge coverage ratio of at least 1.1x.&nbsp; At December 26, 2010, excess availability was $157.6 million and we were in compliance with all covenants of the Revolver. Other covenants include, but are not limited to: limitations on additional debt incurred, mergers, consolidations, or sales, and transactions with subsidiaries and related parties.&nbsp; Failure to meet compliance with one or more of these covenants in the future could affect the amount of availability we have to borrow against and as a result, our liquidity and financial condition may be affected.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: -0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: -0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">(1)&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Debt obligations include the U.S. dollar revolving line of credit and interest bearing obligations to certain former members of Tatum.&nbsp; The future maturity of the U.S. dollar revolving line of credit balance is presented in&nbsp;2014, the year of scheduled maturity, although the revolving line of credit is classified as a current debt obligation in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheet in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles.&nbsp; These amounts primarily include estimated interest, letter of credit fees and unused line fees based on current rates as the balance was largely repaid as of year-end 2010.</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: -0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">(2)&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Operating lease obligations for rent and equipment are expected to be offset by future sublease income of $0.2&nbsp;million in 2011, $0.1 million in 2012 and $0.1 million in 2013. </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: -0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">(3)&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Purchase obligations include normal and customary contracts and minimum spend contracts in the ordinary course of business, primarily information technology outsourcing and maintenance contracts.</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: -0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">(4)&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Other liabilities include the final installment of acquisition consideration for a 2007 transaction and obligations related to the acquisition of Tatum.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements</FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">As of December 26, 2010, we had $31.9 million in irrevocable letters of credit outstanding, which were issued primarily for the benefit of certain insurance carriers to guarantee payment for various self-insurance programs such as workers&#146; compensation insurance.&nbsp; As of December 26, 2010, none of these irrevocable letters of credit had been drawn upon. </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; BACKGROUND: white"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">We do not have any other significant off-balance sheet arrangements.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Critical Accounting Policies</FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The preparation of financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues, expenses and the disclosure of contingencies.&nbsp; Due to the inherent uncertainty involved in making estimates, actual results reported in future periods may be materially different from those estimates.&nbsp; The following policies are those that we consider to be the most critical.&nbsp; See Note&nbsp;1, &#147;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies,&#148; for further description of these and all other accounting policies. </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Allowance for Doubtful Accounts</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;</FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Management analyzes aged receivables and the related allowance for doubtful accounts on a quarterly basis.&nbsp; We use historical experience in assessing the adequacy of the reserve which&nbsp;includes reviewing: net write-offs in relation to revenues, the allowance in comparison to the gross accounts receivable balance and comparative agings.&nbsp; Receivables deemed by management to be uncollectible based on historical trends are reserved for and/or consequently written-off.&nbsp; Historically, losses from uncollectible accounts have not exceeded our allowance.&nbsp; Due to the judgment used in making these assumptions, the ultimate amount of accounts receivable that become uncollectible could differ from our original estimate due to a changing economy or a change in our customers&#146; financial positions, which could result in charges or credits to amounts recorded in selling, general and administrative expenses. </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" face="Times New Roman">29</FONT></P>
<HR color=#808080 SIZE=3 width="100%">
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<DIV></DIV>
<A name="page_33"></A>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;</FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">As required by </FONT><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Accounting Standards Codification No. 350 (ASC 350), (Statement of Financial Accounting Standards (&#147;SFAS&#148;) No.&nbsp;142, &#147;Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets&#148;),</FONT></I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> goodwill and other intangible assets with indefinite lives are not amortized, but are tested for impairment on an annual basis, or earlier if an event occurs or circumstances change that would reduce the fair value of a reporting unit below its carrying amount.&nbsp; For the purposes of our ASC 350 impairment testing, our reporting units are the same as our operating segments, Professional and Staffing Services.&nbsp; Performing an impairment test involves estimating the fair value of a reporting unit. If the carrying amount of a reporting unit exceeds its fair value, then the amount of the impairment loss must be measured. The impairment loss is calculated by comparing the implied fair value of the reporting unit&#146;s goodwill to its carrying amount. In calculating the implied fair value of the reporting unit&#146;s goodwill, the fair value of the reporting unit is allocated to all of the assets and liabilities of the reporting unit. The excess of the fair value of a reporting unit over the amount assigned to its other assets and liabilities is the implied value of goodwill. An impairment loss is recognized when the carrying amount of goodwill exceeds its implied fair value.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN performed its annual impairment test of goodwill&nbsp;as of October 2010.&nbsp; Based on the results of our annual impairment testing, the fair values of our reporting units at October 2010, exceeded their carrying values by a significant&nbsp;margin.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">The impairment test for other intangible</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> assets not subject to amortization consists of a comparison of the fair value of the intangible asset with its carrying value. If the carrying value of the intangible asset exceeds its fair value, an impairment loss is recognized. The estimates of fair value of intangibles not subject to amortization are determined using various discounted cash flow valuation methodologies. Significant assumptions are inherent in this process, including estimates of discount rates. Changes in these assumptions may have a material impact on the financial statements.&nbsp; The results of SFN&#146;s impairment test indicated that no adjustments to the carrying amounts of its non-amortizing intangible assets were required.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=blue face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Impairment of long-lived assets</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;Long-lived assets, primarily fixed assets and other intangible assets, are evaluated by SFN in accordance with ASC 360 </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">(SFAS No. 144 &#147;Accounting for the Impairment of Long-lived Assets&#148;)</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">, whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying value of such assets may not be recoverable.&nbsp; SFN evaluates the fair value of its long-lived assets using an undiscounted cash flow analysis to estimate the assets&#146; fair value. If the estimated future cash flows are projected to be less than the carrying value, an impairment write-down would be recorded, measured by the amount of the assets&#146; carrying value in excess of fair value. Based on SFN&#146;s evaluation, there were no events or changes in circumstances that indicated that the value of the assets were not recoverable.&nbsp; In addition, the remaining useful lives of long-lived assets are reviewed annually.&nbsp; Based on SFN&#146;s evaluation, there were no changes to the remaining useful lives of the long-lived assets.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Accrued self-insurance losses</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;We retain a portion of the risk under our workers' compensation, general liability, professional liability, employment practices liability and health benefits insurance programs.&nbsp; Recording reserves for self-insured losses involves a considerable amount of judgment.&nbsp; In developing the reserves, we use the assistance of actuaries to estimate most of our accruals under the following circumstances: (i) when the accruals are sufficiently material, (ii) when there is an adequate population of claims upon which to prepare actuarial estimates and (iii) when the claims develop over a longer period of time. For all other accruals we base our reserves on internal estimates.&nbsp; Estimated losses for workers' compensation have been discounted at 2.25% and 2.73% as of December 26, 2010 and December 27, 2009, respectively. While management believes that the amount recorded for the liabilities is adequate, there can be no assurance that changes to management&#146;s estimates may not occur due to limitations inherent in the estimation process.&nbsp; Factors that can affect our reserves are as follows:</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: -0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.75in"><FONT style="TEXT-AUTOSPACE: ideograph-numeric; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face=Symbol>&#183;</FONT><FONT style="TEXT-AUTOSPACE: ideograph-numeric; FONT-SIZE: 7pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="TEXT-AUTOSPACE: ideograph-numeric; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">The cost of benefits under the workers' compensation programs are regulated under state law and are subject to change.&nbsp; Legislation can have a significant impact on&nbsp;our ability to control costs&nbsp;related to the amount and frequency of service, the amount of benefits paid if the employee is unable to work and our ability to put the employee back to work.&nbsp; As legislation changes, our estimated liabilities will change.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="TEXT-AUTOSPACE: ideograph-numeric; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: -0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.75in"><FONT style="TEXT-AUTOSPACE: ideograph-numeric; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face=Symbol>&#183;</FONT><FONT style="TEXT-AUTOSPACE: ideograph-numeric; FONT-SIZE: 7pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="TEXT-AUTOSPACE: ideograph-numeric; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Loss estimates from actuaries are primarily based on the historical pattern of losses, including both the frequency and severity of claims.&nbsp; Changes in loss patterns must often be consistently exhibited over a period of time before they are fully reflected in the reserves.&nbsp; Claims can also take a number of years to fully develop&nbsp;until the final loss is known.&nbsp; Changes to estimated loss reserve levels can occur several years after the loss has occurred.&nbsp; A 10% change in either the frequency or severity of claims for one year at current activity levels would impact workers&#146; compensation expense by approximately $1.3 million.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 3pt"><FONT style="TEXT-AUTOSPACE: ideograph-numeric; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: -0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.75in"><FONT style="TEXT-AUTOSPACE: ideograph-numeric; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face=Symbol>&#183;</FONT><FONT style="TEXT-AUTOSPACE: ideograph-numeric; FONT-SIZE: 7pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="TEXT-AUTOSPACE: ideograph-numeric; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Changes in the cost of health care services, claims processing costs, or increased litigation could affect the adequacy of these estimated liabilities.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: -0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.75in" align=center><FONT size=2>30</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=red face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Management reviews these assumptions and related reserves and changes in the estimates of these accruals are charged or credited to cost of services for billable temporary staff and/or selling, general and administrative expenses for branch and administrative staff in the period determined.&nbsp; The Company monitors the impact of reserve changes on its results of operations and over time such reserve changes tend to be insignificant to overall gross profits.&nbsp; During 2010, our workers&#146; compensation and other insurance costs were increased by $4.5 million and decreased by $1.7 million during 2009, for adjustments to prior </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">year reserves and the discount rate.</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=red face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN provides letters of credit to its workers&#146; compensation insurance carrier and various states to collateralize obligations for outstanding claims.&nbsp; SFN also provides cash deposits to various transaction processing vendors (&#147;Other current assets&#148; in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets).&nbsp; The letters of credit and insurance deposits were $31.9 million and $0.3 million at December 26, 2010, respectively, and $37.0 million and $0.4 million at December 27, 2009, respectively</FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Share&#8209;Based Compensation</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">We recognize compensation expense for all share-based payments by estimating the fair value of restricted stock units and stock options at grant date.&nbsp; The fair value of stock options is estimated using the Black-Scholes-Merton option-pricing model.&nbsp; Calculating the fair value of share-based payment awards requires the input of subjective assumptions, including the expected life of the share-based payment awards and stock price volatility.&nbsp; Management bases expected life on historical exercise and post-vesting employment-termination experience, and expected volatility on historical realized volatility trends.&nbsp; In addition, we are required to estimate the expected forfeiture rate and only recognize expense for those shares expected to vest.&nbsp; The assumptions used in calculating the fair value of share-based payment awards represent management&#146;s best estimates, but these estimates involve inherent uncertainties and the application of management&#146;s judgment.&nbsp; As a result, if factors change and we use different assumptions, our share-based compensation expense could be materially different in the future.&nbsp; See Note 2, &#147;Share-Based Compensation&#148; to the Consolidated Financial Statements for a further discussion on share-based compensation.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Income Taxes</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;Deferred tax assets and liabilities are determined based on the difference between the financial statements and tax basis of assets and liabilities using enacted tax rates in effect for the year in which the differences are expected to reverse.&nbsp; Our provision for income taxes is based on domestic and international statutory income tax rates and tax planning opportunities in the jurisdictions in which we operate.&nbsp; Significant judgment is required in determining income tax provisions as well as deferred tax asset and liability balances, including the estimation of valuation allowances and the evaluation of tax positions.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; At December 26, 2010, we had a net deferred tax asset of $137.0&nbsp;million, net of a valuation allowance of </FONT><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">$</FONT></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">5.8 million.&nbsp; Net deferred tax assets are primarily comprised of net deductible temporary differences, net operating loss carryforwards and tax credit carryforwards that are available to reduce taxable income in future periods.&nbsp; The net deferred tax asset was evaluated under the guidelines of ASC 740 </FONT><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">(SFAS No.&nbsp;109, &#147;Accounting for Income Taxes&#148;)</FONT></I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> and a determination on the basis of objective factors was made that the asset will be realized through future years&#146; taxable earnings.&nbsp; These objective factors include historical taxable income, normalized for non-recurring income and expense items.&nbsp; The determination of the amount of valuation allowance to be provided on recorded deferred tax assets involves estimates regarding the timing and amount of the reversal of taxable temporary differences, expected future taxable income and the impact of tax planning strategies.&nbsp; A valuation allowance is required when it is more likely than not that all or a portion of a deferred tax asset will not be realized.&nbsp; In assessing a valuation allowance, we consider all positive and negative evidence available at the time, including past operating results, projections of future taxable income and the feasibility of ongoing tax planning strategies.&nbsp; The current valuation allowance relates primarily to foreign tax credit carryforwards, the benefit on capital loss carryforwards and the benefit on state net operating loss carryforwards that are not expected to be realized.&nbsp; If we determine that future taxable earnings will be insufficient to recover the deferred tax assets, we will be required to write-off all or a portion of the remaining net deferred tax assets by a charge to earnings.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always"></DIV>
<DIV>&nbsp;</DIV>
<A name="page_35"></A><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We are subject to tax audits in numerous jurisdictions in the U.S. and Canada.&nbsp; Tax audits by their very nature are often complex and can require several years to complete.&nbsp; In the normal course of business, we are subject to challenges from the Internal Revenue Service (&#147;IRS&#148;) and other tax authorities regarding amounts of taxes due.&nbsp; These challenges may alter the timing or amount of taxable income or deductions, or the allocation of income among tax jurisdictions.&nbsp; As part of our calculation of the provision for income taxes on earnings, we determine whether the benefits of our tax positions are at least more likely than not of being sustained upon audit based on the technical merits of the tax position.&nbsp; For tax positions that are more likely than not of being sustained upon audit, we accrue the largest amount of the benefit that is more likely than not of being sustained in our Consolidated Financial Statements.&nbsp; Such accruals require management to make estimates and judgments with respect to the ultimate outcome of a tax audit.&nbsp; Actual results could vary materially from these estimates.</FONT>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; See Note 3, &#147;Income Taxes,&#148; in the accompanying notes to the Consolidated Financial Statement for further discussion on income taxes.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">New Accounting Pronouncements</FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; See Note&nbsp;1, &#147;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies,&#148; in the accompanying notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for discussion of New Accounting Pronouncements.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Inflation</FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Our monetary assets, consisting primarily of cash and accounts receivable, are not affected by inflation </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">because they are short-term. Our non-monetary assets, consisting primarily of&nbsp;intangible assets, and prepaid expenses and other assets, are not affected significantly by inflation. We believe that replacement costs of equipment, furniture and leasehold improvements will not materially affect our operations. However, the rate of&nbsp;inflation affects our cost of service and expenses, such as those for employee compensation, which may not be readily recoverable in the price of services offered by us. </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; This Annual Report on Form 10-K includes information extracted from consolidated financial information but not required by generally accepted accounting principles (&#147;GAAP&#148;) to be presented in the financial statements.&nbsp; Certain of this information are considered &#147;non-GAAP financial measures&#148; as defined by SEC rules.&nbsp; Specifically, adjusted</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> earnings from continuing operations is a non-GAAP financial measure which excludes impairment of goodwill and other intangibles, restructuring and other charges related to acquisitions and other cost reduction initiatives, and adjustments to tax valuation allowances. Adjusted earnings from continuing operations are key measures used by management to evaluate its operations.&nbsp; Non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered a measure of financial performance in isolation or as an alternative to revenue growth as determined in the Statement of Operations in accordance with GAAP, and, as presented, may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies, and therefore this measure has material limitations.&nbsp; Non-GAAP financial measures should be considered in addition to, but not as a substitute for or superior to, other measures of financial performance prepared in accordance with GAAP.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Forward Looking Statements&#151;Safe&nbsp; Harbor</FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows and prospects, and the prevailing market price and performance of our common stock, may be adversely affected by a number of factors, including the matters discussed below. The risks, uncertainties and other factors that our stockholders and prospective investors should consider are included in Item 1A, Risk Factors.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: -0.75in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.75in"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Item 7A.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK</FONT></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
<A name="QuanandQual"></A>SFN is exposed to interest rate risk related to a portion of its debt.&nbsp; The outstanding variable-rate debt was $0.05 million and $10.8 million at December 26, 2010 and December 27, 2009, respectively.&nbsp; Based on the outstanding balances in 2010 and 2009, a change of 1% in the interest rate would have caused a change in interest expense of an immaterial amount in 2010 and $0.1 million in 2009.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=red face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=red face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">From time to time, we participate in foreign exchange hedging activities to mitigate the impact of changes in foreign currency exchange rates.&nbsp; We attempt to hedge transaction exposures through natural offsets.&nbsp; To the extent this is not practicable, exposure areas which are considered for hedging are foreign currency denominated receivables and payables, intercompany loans and firm committed transactions.&nbsp; We use financial instruments, principally forward exchange contracts, in our management of foreign currency exposures related to our Canadian operations.&nbsp; We do not enter into forward contracts for trading purposes.&nbsp; In estimating the fair value of derivative positions, we utilize quoted market prices, if available, or quotes obtained from external sources.&nbsp; As of December 26, 2010, we had one outstanding forward contract to sell CAD $6.2 million in January 2011. The Canadian hedge is expected to remain outstanding until the Canadian intercompany loan is repaid. This derivative had a fair value or cost to unwind that is not material to our consolidated results of operations. </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><FONT size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><FONT size=2>33</FONT></P>
<HR color=#808080 SIZE=3 width="100%">
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=red face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">When foreign currency financial instruments are outstanding, exposure to market risk on these instruments results from fluctuations in currency rates during the periods in which the contracts are outstanding.&nbsp; The counterparties to our currency exchange contracts consist of major financial institutions, each of which is rated investment grade. SFN provides letters of credit to its workers&#146; compensation insurance carrier and various states to collateralize obligations for outstanding claims.&nbsp; The cost of the letters of credit is based on a margin as determined by an interest rate grid, plus a fixed fronting fee of 12.5 basis points, which is subject to availability under the U.S. credit facility. The letters of credit were $31.9 million and $37.0 million at December 26, 2010 and December 27, 2009, respectively.&nbsp; We are exposed to credit risk to the extent of potential nonperformance by counterparties on financial instruments.&nbsp; Any potential credit exposure does not exceed the fair value.&nbsp; We believe the risk of incurring losses due to credit risk is remote. </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The carrying amount of cash and cash equivalents, trade receivables and other current assets approximates fair value due to the short-term maturities of these instruments. The fair values of all other financial instruments, including debt, approximate their book values as the instruments are short-term in nature or contain market rates of interest. </FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Management&#146;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</FONT></B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
<A name="ManagementsReport"></A>Management is responsible for the fair presentation of the Consolidated Financial Statements of SFN Group, Inc.&nbsp; Management is also responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting as defined in Rule&nbsp;13a-15(f) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.&nbsp; Our internal control system is designed to provide reasonable assurance that the reported financial information is presented fairly, that disclosures are adequate and that the judgments inherent in the preparation of financial statements are reasonable.&nbsp; There are inherent limitations in the effectiveness of any system of internal control, including the possibility of human error and overriding of controls.&nbsp; Consequently, an effective internal control system can only provide reasonable, not absolute assurance, with respect to reporting financial information.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Management conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting based on the framework in </FONT><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Internal Control&#8209;Integrated Framework</FONT></I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.&nbsp; Based on our evaluation under the framework in </FONT><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Internal Control&#8209;Integrated Framework,</FONT></I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> management concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December 26, 2010.</FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Deloitte &amp; Touche LLP, the independent registered public accounting firm that audited the financial statements included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, has issued an attestation report on our internal control over financial reporting, such attestation report is included herein.</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</FONT></B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">To the Board of Directors and Stockholders of</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN Group, Inc.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Fort Lauderdale, Florida</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">We have audited the internal control over financial reporting of SFN Group, Inc. and subsidiaries (the "Company") as of December 26, 2010, based on criteria established in </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Internal Control &#151; Integrated Framework </FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.&nbsp; The Company's management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting and for its assessment of the effectivenness of internal control over financial reporting, included in the accompanying Management's Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting.&nbsp; Our responsibilty is to express an opinion on the Company's internal control over financial reporting based on our audit.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT size=2></FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects. Our audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk, and performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">A company's internal control over financial reporting is a process designed by, or under the supervision of, the company's principal executive and principal financial officers, or persons performing similar functions, and effected by the company's board of directors, management, and other personnel to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company's internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company's assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Because of the inherent limitations of internal control over financial reporting, including the possibility of collusion or improper management override of controls, material misstatements due to error or fraud may not be prevented or detected on a timely basis. Also, projections of any evaluation of the effectiveness of the internal control over financial reporting to future periods are subject to the risk that the controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">In our opinion, the Company maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 26, 2010, based on the criteria established in </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Internal Control &#151; Integrated Framework </FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission. </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">We have also audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), the consolidated financial statements and financial statement schedule as of and for the year ended December 26, 2010 of the Company and our report dated March&nbsp;4, 2011 expressed an unqualified opinion on those financial statements and financial statement schedule.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">DELOITTE&nbsp;&amp; TOUCHE LLP</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Certified Public Accountants</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Miami, Florida</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">March 4,&nbsp;2011</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
