<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of SFN Group, Inc. and subsidiaries (the "Company") as of December 26, 2010 and December 27, 2009, and the related consolidated statements of operations, stockholders&#146; equity, and cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 26, 2010. Our audits also included the consolidated financial statement schedule listed in the Index at Item 15. These financial statements and consolidated financial statement schedule are the responsibility of the Company's management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the financial statements and financial statement schedule based on our audits.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. An audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">In our opinion, such consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of SFN Group, Inc. and subsidiaries as of December 26, 2010 and December 27, 2009, and the results of their operations and their cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 26, 2010, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. Also, in our opinion, such financial statement schedule, when considered in relation to the basic consolidated financial statements taken as a whole, presents fairly, in all material respects, the information set forth therein.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">We have also audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), the Company's internal control over financial reporting as of December 26, 2010, based on the criteria established in <I>Internal Control&#151;Integrated Framework </I>issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission and our report dated March 4, 2011, expressed an unqualified opinion on the Company's internal control over financial reporting.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES</FONT></B></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center>
<A name="NotestoFinan"></A><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</FONT></B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">1.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</FONT></B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
<A name="SOSAP"></A>Business&#151;</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN Group, Inc.,(&#147;SFN&#148; or the &#147;Company&#148;) formerly Spherion Corporation, is a strategic workforce solutions provider founded in 1946.&nbsp; SFN is headquartered in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, and operates a network of 559 locations within the United States of America and Canada. &nbsp;The Company has two operating segments, Professional Services and Staffing Services, which provide temporary staffing, outsourcing and other services and permanent placement under several specialty brands. Temporary staffing includes placing our employees at a customer location under the customer&#146;s supervision in the following skill categories: information technology, finance and accounting, administrative, legal, engineering, sales and marketing, human resources, light industrial and clerical.&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Outsourcing and other includes services where we manage aspects of the operation of a customer function such as recruiting, contingent labor management, independent contractor compliance and professional payrolling; where services are typically provided under long-term contracts.&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Permanent placement is a service where we locate talent on behalf of our customers, screen the candidates and assist in the recruitment efforts for a fee.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face=Arial></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Consolidation Policy</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;The accompanying Consolidated Financial Statements include the accounts of SFN, its wholly&#8209;owned subsidiaries and certain other entities it is required to consolidate.&nbsp; All intercompany transactions and balances have been eliminated.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">In accordance with ASC 810 </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">(SFAS No.167 &#147;Amendments to FASB Interpretation No. 46(R)&#148;),</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN consolidates variable interest entities (VIE&#146;s) for which it is the primary beneficiary.&nbsp; SFN has evaluated the provisions of ASC 810 and determined that it applies to its franchise agreements.&nbsp; SFN has determined that these agreements by themselves do not create a VIE, but in some cases SFN has provided loans under these agreements which may create a VIE.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=red face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">VIE&#146;s are generally entities that lack sufficient equity to operate without additional subordinated financial support from other parties or are entities whose equity holders do not have adequate decision making authority.&nbsp; SFN, in cases when financing support is provided to a franchisee, must evaluate whether or not it is the primary beneficiary. The primary beneficiary of a VIE is the party that (a) has the power to direct the activities of a VIE that significantly impacts its economic performance and (b) has the obligation to absorb the losses or the rights to receive the benefits that could be significant to the VIE. </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=red face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=red face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN&#146;s VIE consolidated net assets were $0.5 million and $1.1 million at December 26, 2010 and December 27, 2009, respectively.&nbsp; Each franchisee&#146;s loan is collateralized by its respective business and in the event of default on the loan, SFN retains the right to take over the franchisee&#146;s operations.&nbsp; General creditors of SFN&#146;s franchisees do not have any recourse against SFN.&nbsp; All net assets are included in &#147;Other current assets&#148; in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets</FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=red face="Times New Roman">.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Use of Estimates</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period.&nbsp; Due to the inherent uncertainty involved in making estimates, actual results reported in future periods may be materially different from those estimates</FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">. </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Fiscal Year</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;SFN&#146;s fiscal year is comprised of the 52 or 53 weeks ending on the last Sunday in December.&nbsp; The fiscal years ended on December 26, 2010 (&#147;fiscal year 2010&#148; or &#147;2010&#148;), December 27, 2009 and December 28, 2008, all contained 52 weeks.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Cash and Cash Equivalents</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;All highly liquid investments with original maturities of 90&nbsp;days or less at the time of purchase are classified as cash equivalents.&nbsp; Cash equivalents are carried at cost, which approximates fair value due to the short-term maturities of these instruments. </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">43</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>

<DIV>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><B><FONT style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES</FONT></B></FONT></B></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><B><FONT style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS- (Continued)</FONT></B></FONT></B></P>
</DIV>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">1.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (Continued)</FONT></B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Allowance for Doubtful Accounts</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;Accounts receivable are carried at the amount estimated to be collectible.&nbsp; Accordingly, allowances are provided for accounts receivable estimated to be uncollectible based on management&#146;s best estimates based on historical write-off levels and other factors.&nbsp; Accounts receivable are written-off in the period they are deemed uncollectible and recoveries are recognized in the period they are received.&nbsp; The actual amount of accounts receivable that become uncollectible could differ from those estimated.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Investments</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;SFN invests in mutual funds in an amount approximately equal to its obligation to employees pursuant to the terms of its non-qualified deferred compensation plans (See Note 10, &#147;Employee Savings and Investment Plans&#148;).&nbsp; These investments are classified as trading securities and are reported at fair value with gains and losses included in earnings during the period incurred.&nbsp; Fair value is determined based on quoted prices in active markets, Level I of the fair value hierarchy.&nbsp; The specific identification method is used to determine the cost of investments sold.&nbsp; These investments are included in &#147;Other current assets&#148; and &#147;Other assets&#148; in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets</FONT></I></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;</FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> As required by ASC 350, </FONT><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">(Statement of Financial Accounting Standards (&#147;SFAS&#148;) No.&nbsp;142, &#147;Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets&#148;),</FONT></I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> goodwill and other intangible assets with indefinite lives are not amortized, but are tested for impairment on an annual basis, or earlier if an event occurs or circumstances change that would reduce the fair value of a reporting unit below its carrying amount. For the purposes of our ASC 350 impairment testing, our reporting units are the same as our operating segments, Professional and Staffing Services.&nbsp; Performing an impairment test involves estimating the fair value of a reporting unit. If the carrying amount of a reporting unit exceeds its fair value, then the amount of the impairment loss must be measured. The impairment loss is calculated by comparing the implied fair value of the reporting unit&#146;s goodwill to its carrying amount. In calculating the implied fair value of the reporting unit&#146;s goodwill, the fair value of the reporting unit is allocated to all of the assets and liabilities of the reporting unit. The excess of the fair value of a reporting unit over the amount assigned to its other assets and liabilities is the implied value of goodwill. An impairment loss is recognized when the carrying amount of goodwill exceeds its implied fair value. </FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">As of December 26, 2010, goodwill allocated to each of the reporting units, Professional Services and Staffing Services was $30.6 million and $0.5 million, respectively. SFN performed its annual impairment test of goodwill&nbsp;as of October 2010.&nbsp; Based on the results of our annual impairment testing, the fair value of our reporting units at October 2010, exceeded their carrying amounts by a significant&nbsp;margin.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">The impairment test for other intangible</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> assets not subject to amortization consists of a comparison of the fair value of the intangible asset with its carrying value. If the carrying value of the intangible asset exceeds its fair value, an impairment loss is recognized. The estimates of fair value of intangibles not subject to amortization are determined using various discounted cash flow valuation methodologies. Significant assumptions are inherent in this process, including estimates of discount rates. Changes in these assumptions may have a material impact on the financial statements.&nbsp; The results of SFN&#146;s impairment tests indicated that no adjustment to the carrying amounts of its&#146; non-amortizing intangible assets were required.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Property and Equipment</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;Property and equipment are stated at cost and depreciated using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the related assets.&nbsp; Leasehold improvements are amortized over the shorter of their estimated useful life or the lease term using the straight-line method.&nbsp; Maintenance and repairs, which do not improve or extend the life of an asset, are expensed as incurred. </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Capitalized Software Costs</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;Software which has been developed for internal use is accounted for in accordance with ASC 350, </FONT><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">(Statement of Position (&#147;SOP&#148;) 98-1, &#147;Accounting for the Costs of Computer Software Developed or Obtained for Internal Use&#148;).&nbsp; </FONT></I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;Only costs incurred during the application development stage, including design, coding, installation and testing are capitalized.&nbsp; These capitalized costs include external consulting fees, software license fees and internal labor costs for employees directly associated with software development.&nbsp; Upgrades or modifications that result in additional functionality are capitalized, while upgrades or modifications that do not result in additional functionality are expensed as incurred. </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><FONT size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><B><FONT style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES</FONT></B></FONT></B></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><B><FONT style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS- (Continued)</FONT></B></FONT></B></P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">1.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (Continued)</FONT></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;As required by ASC 360 </FONT><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">(SFAS No.&nbsp;144, &#147;Accounting for the Impairment or Disposal of Long-Lived Assets&#148;)</FONT></I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">, long-lived assets should be tested for recoverability whenever events or circumstances indicate that their carrying amount may not be recoverable.&nbsp; If such circumstances existed, </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN would evaluate the fair value of its long-lived assets using an undiscounted cash flow analysis to estimate the assets&#146; fair value. If the estimated future cash flows are projected to be less than the carrying value, an impairment loss would be recorded, measured by the amount of the assets&#146; carrying value in excess of fair value. Based on SFN&#146;s evaluation, there were no events or changes in circumstances that indicated that the value of the assets were not recoverable. In addition, the remaining useful lives of long-lived assets are reviewed annually.&nbsp; Based on SFN&#146;s evaluation, there were no changes to the remaining useful lives of the long-lived assets.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Accrued Self-Insurance Losses</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;SFN retains a portion of the risk under its workers&#146; compensation, general liability, professional liability, employment practices liability and health benefits insurance programs.&nbsp; Estimated losses for workers&#146; compensation have been discounted at 2.25% and 2.73% at December 26, 2010 and December 27, 2009, respectively.&nbsp; While management believes that the amount recorded for the liabilities is adequate, there can be no assurance that changes to management&#146;s estimates may not occur due to limitations inherent in the estimation process.&nbsp; Changes in the estimates of these accruals are charged or credited to earnings in the period determined.&nbsp; SFN provides letters of credit to its workers&#146; compensation insurance carrier and various states to collateralize obligations for outstanding claims.&nbsp; SFN also provides cash deposits to various transaction processing vendors (Included in &#147;Other current assets&#148; in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets).&nbsp;&nbsp; The letters of credit and insurance deposits were $31.9 million and $0.3 million at December 26, 2010, respectively, and $37.0 million and $0.4 million at December 27, 2009, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Fair Value of Financial Instruments</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;SFN&#146;s financial instruments consists of cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivable, accounts payable, and long-term debt. The carrying amounts of cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivable and accounts payable approximate their fair values based on their short-term nature. The recorded values of long-term debt approximate their fair value, as interest approximates market rates.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Foreign Currency Translation</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;SFN&#146;s Canadian operation uses the Canadian dollar as its functional currency.&nbsp; Assets and liabilities of this operation are translated at the exchange rates in effect on the balance sheet date.&nbsp; Amounts included in SFN&#146;s Consolidated Statements of Operations are translated at the average exchange rates for the year.&nbsp; The impact of currency fluctuation is included in stockholders&#146; equity as part of accumulated other comprehensive income. </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Revenue Recognition</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;SFN records revenues from sales of services by its company&#8209;owned and franchised operations and from royalties earned on sales of services by its area-based franchised operations.&nbsp; Temporary staffing revenues and the related labor costs are recorded in the period in which services are performed.&nbsp; Permanent placement revenues are recognized upon candidate start date.&nbsp; Allowances are established to estimate losses due to placed candidates not remaining employed for SFN&#146;s guarantee period.&nbsp; SFN also enters into agreements with its customers to provide Recruitment Process Outsourcing (&#147;RPO&#148;) in which the recruitment functions of the customer are provided by SFN.&nbsp; Revenues are recognized when services are delivered and to the extent that amounts are non-refundable under the terms of the agreement.&nbsp; Sales tax collected from customers and remitted to the applicable taxing authorities is accounted for on a net basis, with no impact on revenues.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; SFN follows ASC 605 </FONT><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">(Emerging Issues Task Force (&#147;EITF&#148;) 99-19, &#147;Reporting Revenue Gross as a Principal versus Net as an Agent&#148;),</FONT></I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> in the presentation of revenues and expenses.&nbsp; This guidance requires SFN to assess whether it acts as a principal in the transaction or as an agent acting on behalf of others.&nbsp; In situations where SFN is the principal in the transaction and has the risks and rewards of ownership, the transactions are recorded gross in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.&nbsp; When we act as an agent, such as in cases where we provide service using a third-party vendor, we report the revenues on a net basis and the corresponding receivable from the client and liability to the vendor.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" face="Times New Roman">45</FONT></P>
<HR color=#808080 SIZE=3 width="100%">
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center>&nbsp;</P>

<A name="page_49"></A>
<DIV>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><B><FONT style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES</FONT></B></FONT></B></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><B><FONT style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS- (Continued)</FONT></B></FONT></B></P>
</DIV>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">1.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (Continued)</FONT></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; SFN utilizes two forms of franchising agreements.&nbsp; Under the first form, SFN records area-based franchise royalties in accordance with ASC 952, </FONT><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">(SFAS No.&nbsp;45, &#147;Accounting for Franchise Fee Revenue&#148;),</FONT></I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">based upon the contractual percentage of area-based franchise sales in the period in which the area-based franchisee provides the service.&nbsp; Area-based franchise royalties, which are included in revenues, were $5.1&nbsp;million, $4.3 million, and $6.3&nbsp;million for the 2010, 2009 and 2008 fiscal years, respectively.&nbsp; The second form of franchising agreement is a franchise agreement where SFN acts as the principal in customer transactions through direct contractual relationships with the customers, owning related customer receivables and being the legal employer of the temporary employee and the franchisee acts as SFN&#146;s agent providing certain sales and recruiting services.&nbsp; Accordingly, sales and costs of services generated by the second form of franchised operations are recorded in SFN&#146;s Consolidated Statements of Operations.&nbsp; SFN pays the franchisee a commission for acting as SFN&#146;s agent and this commission is based on a percentage of gross profit from the office managed by the franchisee and averaged 74%, 75% and 74% for the fiscal years ended 2010, 2009 and 2008, respectively.&nbsp; The franchisee is responsible for establishing its office location and paying related administrative and operating expenses, such as rent, utilities and salaries of the franchisee&#146;s sales and service employees. </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Except in circumstances where SFN is required to consolidate certain franchisees' operations in accordance with ASC 810,&nbsp;</FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN&#146;s Consolidated Statements of Operations reflect franchisee commission as an expense, but does not include the rent, utilities and salaries of the franchisee&#146;s full-time office employees as these expenses are the responsibility of the franchisee.&nbsp; SFN has credit risk for sales to its customers through franchisee arrangements as SFN pays all direct costs associated with providing temporary services before related accounts receivable are collected.&nbsp; SFN has partially mitigated this risk by making the franchisee responsible to reimburse SFN up to 100% of uncollected accounts receivable (bad debts are deducted from commission payments); however, SFN bears the loss in cases where the franchisee does not have sufficient financial wherewithal to reimburse uncollected amounts. </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Income Taxes</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;Deferred taxes arise from temporary differences between the tax basis of an asset or liability and its reported amount in the Consolidated Financial Statements.&nbsp; Valuation allowances on deferred tax assets are recorded to the extent it is more likely than not that a tax benefit will not be realized.&nbsp; SFN is subject to tax audits in numerous jurisdictions in the U.S. and Canada.&nbsp; Tax audits by their very nature are often complex and can require several years to complete.&nbsp; In the normal course of business, SFN is subject to challenges from the Internal Revenue Service (&#147;IRS&#148;) and other tax authorities regarding amounts of taxes due.&nbsp; These challenges may alter the timing or amount of taxable income or deductions, or the allocation of income among tax jurisdictions.&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Effective January 1, 2007, SFN adopted ASC 740 </FONT><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">(FASB Interpretation No. (FIN) 48, &#147;Accounting for Uncertainty in Income Taxes&#148;).&nbsp; </FONT></I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">ASC 740 requires that SFN determine whether the benefits of its tax positions are more likely than not of being sustained upon audit based on the technical merits of the tax position.&nbsp; For tax positions that are at least more likely than not of being sustained upon audit, SFN recognizes the largest amount of the benefit that is more likely than not of being sustained in SFN&#146;s Consolidated Financial Statements.&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Earnings Per Share</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;Basic earnings (loss) per share is computed by dividing&nbsp;earnings (loss) applicable to common shareholders by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during the period.&nbsp; When the effects of the common stock equivalents are not anti-dilutive, diluted earnings per share is computed by dividing&nbsp;net earnings plus after-tax interest on convertible debt, if applicable, by the weighted-average number of shares outstanding and the impact of all dilutive potential common shares, primarily stock options, convertible notes, restricted stock and restricted stock units.&nbsp; The dilutive impact of stock options is determined by applying the &#147;treasury stock&#148; method and the dilutive impact of the convertible notes is determined by applying the &#147;if converted&#148; method.&nbsp; SFN does not currently have any convertible debt outstanding.&nbsp; See Note&nbsp;4, &#147;Earnings (Loss) Per Share,&#148; for further discussion. </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Derivative Financial Instruments</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;From time to time, SFN enters into foreign exchange forward contracts as part of the management of its foreign currency exchange rate exposures.&nbsp; These financial instruments are not held for trading purposes and none of the instruments are leveraged.&nbsp; All financial instruments are put into place to hedge specific exposures.&nbsp; Gains and losses on foreign currency forward contracts offset gains and losses resulting from the underlying transactions.&nbsp; SFN accounts for its derivatives in accordance with ASC 815, </FONT><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">(SFAS No.&nbsp;133, &#147;Accounting for Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities&#148;)</FONT></I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">, as amended.&nbsp; Gains and losses on contracts that hedge foreign currency commitments are recognized in earnings. </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Amounts receivable or payable under the agreements are included in &#147;Other current assets&#148; or &#147;Other current liabilities&#148; in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets. </FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS- (Continued)</FONT></B></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">1.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (Continued)</FONT></B><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> </FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Share&#8209;Based Compensation</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;As required by </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">ASC 718, </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">(</FONT></I><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFAS No. </FONT></I><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">123(R), &#147;Share-Based Payment&#148;)</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">, the measurement and recognition of compensation expense for all share-based payment awards made to employees and directors is based on estimated fair values.&nbsp; The fair values of stock options are measured using an option pricing model.&nbsp; The fair value of deferred stock units and restricted stock units are measured at the market price on the date of grant.&nbsp; The value of awards that are ultimately expected to vest is recognized as expense over the requisite service periods in SFN&#146;s Consolidated Statement of Operations.&nbsp; See Note 2, &#147;Share-Based Compensation,&#148; for further discussion.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">New Accounting Pronouncements and Interpretations</FONT></I></B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#151;SFN adopted the provisions of </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">ASC 810 </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">(SFAS No.167 &#147;Amendments to FASB Interpretation No. 46(R)&#148;).&nbsp;</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">ASC </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">810 requires ongoing reassessments of whether an enterprise is the primary beneficiary of a VIE and also requires an entity to qualitatively assess the determination of the primary beneficiary of a VIE based on whether the entity has (a) the power to direct the significant activities of the VIE and (b) has the obligation to absorb</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> losses or the right to receive benefits of the VIE that could potentially be significant to the VIE. ASC 810 eliminates the quantitative approach previously required to determine the primary beneficiary of a variable interest entity.&nbsp; The adoption of ASC 810 did not have an impact on SFN&#146;s consolidated financial statements. </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">2.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; SHARE&#8209;BASED COMPENSATION </FONT></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In May 2006, SFN&#146;s stockholders approved the adoption of the&nbsp;2006 Stock Incentive Plan, which&nbsp;replaced the 2000 Stock Incentive Plan and the Deferred Stock Plan effective July 1, 2006.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the 2006 Stock Incentive Plan, options to purchase SFN&#146;s common stock and stock appreciation rights may be granted to employees and outside directors of SFN and its subsidiaries for periods not to exceed seven years at a price that is not less than 100% of fair market value on the date of grant.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2006 Stock Incentive Plan also allows for stock-based awards including common stock, performance shares, performance units, restricted stock and restricted stock units, although there are limitations on the amount of full value awards that can be granted. All awards of stock options, restricted stock units and other stock-based awards granted&nbsp;on or after July 1, 2006 will be issued under&nbsp;the 2006 Stock Incentive Plan.&nbsp; As of December 26, 2010, SFN had 423,106 shares reserved for future grants under the 2006 Stock Incentive Plan.&nbsp; Additionally, any shares subject to awards under the 2000 Stock Incentive Plan that are cancelled, forfeited or surrendered will be&nbsp;available for&nbsp;re-grant under the 2006 Stock Incentive Plan.&nbsp; SFN expects to satisfy all of its obligation to issue shares under share-based compensation plans with treasury stock.</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">All share-based compensation expense and tax benefits, primarily related to stock option and restricted stock unit awards, recognized in the Consolidated Statements of Operations during the year were as follows (in thousands):</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">2.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; SHARE&#8209;BASED COMPENSATION (Continued)</FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Stock Options and Employee Stock Purchase Plan</FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Compensation expense for stock options is measured at the fair value of each option grant and is estimated using the Black-Scholes-Merton option pricing model.&nbsp; The fair value is then amortized over the requisite vesting periods of the awards.&nbsp; Stock options vest ratably over a 3 year period based on continued service with the Company.&nbsp; Use of this valuation model requires management to make certain assumptions with respect to selected model inputs.&nbsp; Expected volatility was calculated based on the historical volatility of SFN&#146;s stock.&nbsp; The average expected life was based on the contractual term of the option and expected employee exercise and post-vesting employment termination behavior.&nbsp; The risk-free interest rate is based on U.S. Treasury zero-coupon issues with a remaining term equal to the expected life assumed at the date of grant.&nbsp; Forfeitures are estimated based on historical option forfeiture activity.&nbsp; Assumptions used in the valuation model were as follows:</FONT></P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">As of December 26, 2010, there was approximately $0.9 million of total unrecognized compensation costs related to nonvested stock options granted under the Plan.&nbsp; That cost is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average period of 1.48 years.&nbsp; The total fair value of stock options vested during the year ended December 26, 2010, December 27, 2009 and December 28, 2008 was $1.0 million, $1.7 million, and $1.9 million, respectively.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 25pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Cash received from option exercises was $0.6 million, </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">$0.02&nbsp;million, and $0.1&nbsp;million, for the fiscal years ended December 26, 2010, December 27, 2009 and December 28, 2008, respectively.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 24pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; SFN also has an Employee Stock Purchase Plan that provides substantially all employees who have been employed for at least six months an opportunity to purchase shares of its common stock at a discount of 15%.&nbsp; The provisions of ASC 718 </FONT><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">(SFAS No. 123R) </FONT></I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">require the expense related to SFN&#146;s Employee Stock Purchase Plan be recorded in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">The tax benefit from disqualifying dispositions and employee stock purchase plan totaled $0.06 million, $0.03 million, and $0.01 million, for the fiscal years ended December 26, 2010, December 27, 2009 and December 28, 2008, respectively.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Restricted Stock Units</FONT></I></B></P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN employees</FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> and outside directors are eligible to receive grants of restricted stock units.&nbsp; Restricted stock units entitle the recipient to receive shares of SFN common stock at a future date after the recipient has met service requirements or SFN has met financial targets.&nbsp; The majority of the restricted stock units vest based upon attainment of performance criteria; the remainder vest over 1 to 7 years.&nbsp; If performance criteria are not met, the shares do not vest and recognized compensation cost, if any, is reversed to income.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; SFN has a United States federal net operating loss carryforward in the amount of $90.8&nbsp;million expiring in 2024 and thereafter.&nbsp; SFN has $206.8 million of state net operating loss carryforwards which expire over the next one to twenty years.&nbsp; Canadian net operating loss carryforwards are available in the amount of $2.0&nbsp;million, and expire between 2014 and 2016.&nbsp; The Company also has a capital loss carryforward in the amount of $11.8 million and a carryforward of $30.9 million of&nbsp;general&nbsp;business&nbsp;credits, primarily work opportunity tax credits. The benefits on capital loss carryforwards expire between 2011 and 2015; and general business credits carried forward will expire between 2021 and 2030.</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">3.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; INCOME TAXES (Continued)</FONT></B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; SFN&#146;s valuation allowance decreased by $0.6 million during 2010.&nbsp; The remaining valuation allowance reduces the deferred tax asset to an amount that is more likely than not to be realized, and is based on the uncertainty of the realization of two principal items. First, the exit from most of SFN&#146;s foreign operations makes it unlikely that it will utilize any foreign tax credits in the future.&nbsp; As such, a valuation allowance has been recorded against the full amount of foreign tax credit carryforward of $0.7 million.&nbsp; Second, SFN has recorded a valuation allowance of $2.4 million against the capital loss carryforwards (included with total loss carryforwards of $45.0 million).&nbsp; The benefits on foreign tax credits expire between 2012 and 2015.&nbsp; Valuation allowances for state net operating loss carryforwards and other items account for the remainder of the total $5.8 million.&nbsp; As of December 26, 2010, and December 27, 2009 there were no unremitted foreign earnings.</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=red face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp; SFN files income tax returns in the U.S. federal jurisdiction and most states.&nbsp; SFN also files tax returns in Canada.&nbsp; SFN is no longer subject to U.S. federal, state and local, or non-U.S. income tax examinations by tax authorities for years before 2001.&nbsp; The IRS has completed examinations of SFN&#146;s tax returns through the 2004 tax year, and all adjustments have been recorded.&nbsp; In years 2002 through 2004, however, SFN reported a net operating loss, and those losses will be subject to re-examination in the years in which they are utilized to offset future income. </FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN recognizes interest and penalties accrued with respect to unrecognized tax benefits in income tax expense.&nbsp; The total liability for interest and penalties recorded was $0.5 million at December 26, 2010 and $0.4 million at December 27, 2009 and December 28, 2008.&nbsp; As of December 26, 2010, the balance of unrecognized tax benefits, excluding interest and penalties, was $1.4 million, of which $0.9 million is attributable to state net operating loss carryforwards and was recorded as a reduction to a deferred tax asset.&nbsp; As of December 27, 2009 and December 28, 2008, the balance of unrecognized tax benefits, excluding interest and penalties, was $1.6 million, of which $1.0 million was attributable to state net operating loss carryforwards and was recorded as a reduction to deferred tax asset. Included in the balance of unrecognized tax benefits are $0.9 million, $1.0 million and $1.1 million of tax benefits that, if recognized, would affect the effective tax rate at December 26, 2010, December 27, 2009, and December 28, 2008, respectively.&nbsp; It is a reasonable possibility that the amounts of unrecognized tax benefits will increase or decrease in the next 12 months, but an estimate of such an increase or decrease is not possible.&nbsp; </FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="TEXT-AUTOSPACE: ideograph-numeric; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">The primary reasons the purchase price for Tatum exceeded the fair value of net assets acquired were expected future cash flows, expanded growth opportunities from enhanced service offerings in the office of the CFO and synergies to be realized from the elimination of duplicative administrative activities. This resulted in the recognition of $30.3 million of goodwill, which is deductible for tax purposes.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 26.25pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="TEXT-AUTOSPACE: ideograph-numeric; FONT-SIZE: 9pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="TEXT-AUTOSPACE: ideograph-numeric; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; SFN incurred $3.6 million for transaction and integration costs related to the acquisition of Tatum, which is included in restructuring and other charges in the accompanying Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations. The acquisition of Tatum is not considered a significant acquisition, and as such, proforma financial information has not been provided.</FONT></P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We have a revolving line of credit in the amount of $250 million (the &#147;Revolver&#148;) which is secured by substantially all of SFN&#146;s accounts receivable and provides for U.S. and Canadian dollar borrowings. On October 29, 2010, the Company and its lenders entered into an amendment (the &#147;First Amendment&#148;) to the Amended and Restated Loan and Security Agreement (the &#147;Agreement&#148;), extending the maturity date of the Revolver to November 15, 2014 and reducing the interest rate margins and fees.&nbsp; The First Amendment did not materially change any of the covenants contained in the Revolver.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; As of December 26, 2010, there was $0.05 million outstanding, and as of December 27, 2009, there was $10.8 million outstanding.&nbsp; As of December 26, 2010, total availability was $157.6&nbsp;million (calculated as eligible receivables of $224.1 million, less: borrowings outstanding of $0.05 million, letters of credit of $31.9 million and a one week payroll reserve of $34.6&nbsp;million).&nbsp; The interest rate on this line of credit is based upon the duration of the loan, availability under the line and other conditions and was approximately 4.75% (prime rate plus 1.50% margin) as of December 26, 2010.&nbsp; Pursuant to the terms of the Agreement, we pay an unused line fee in the range of 0.375% to 0.5% per annum that is determined by the unused portion of the revolving line of credit.&nbsp; For letters of credit, we pay an annual rate based on availability under the line (currently 2.5%) plus a fixed fronting fee of 0.125%.&nbsp; For further discussion on letters of credit, see Note 11, &#147;Commitments and Contingencies.&#148;</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 25pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">The Revolver contains certain affirmative and negative covenants, the most significant of which is a minimum fixed charge coverage requirement under certain conditions.&nbsp; If excess availability, as defined by the Agreement, falls below $30.0 million, we are required to maintain a fixed charge coverage ratio of at least 1.1x.&nbsp; At December 26, 2010, excess availability was $157.6 million and we were in compliance with all covenants of the Revolver</FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">. </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Other covenants include, but are not limited to: limitations on additional debt incurred, mergers, consolidations, or sales, and transactions with subsidiaries and related parties.&nbsp; Failure to meet compliance with one or more of these covenants in the future could affect the amount of availability we have to borrow against and as a result, our liquidity and financial condition may be affected.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 25pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">In connection with the purchase of Tatum, SFN assumed interest bearing obligations to certain former members of Tatum of $3.6 million</FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">. The obligations are </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">payable through January 2014 and include interest at an average rate of 5.3%.&nbsp; As of December 26, 2010, the remaining liability balance is approximately $2.1 million.</FONT></P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 25pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-AUTOSPACE: ideograph-numeric; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Aggregate future maturities of long-term debt as of December 26, 2010 are $2.6 million in 2011, $1.6&nbsp;million in 2012, $0.9 million in 2013 and $0.01 million in 2014.&nbsp; These future maturities include the Revolver balance in 2014, although this revolving line of credit is classified as a current debt obligation in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheet in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles.</FONT></P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-AUTOSPACE: ideograph-numeric; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 10pt"><B><FONT style="TEXT-AUTOSPACE: ideograph-numeric; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">9.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS AND FAIR VALUES</FONT></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The fair value of a financial instrument represents the amount at which the instrument could be exchanged in a current transaction between willing parties, other than in a forced or liquidation sale.&nbsp; Fair value estimates are made at a specific point in time, based upon relevant market information about the financial instrument. </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The carrying amount of cash and cash equivalents, trade receivables and all other financial instruments, including debt, approximates fair value as the instruments are short-term in nature or contain market rates of interest. SFN provides letters of credit to its workers&#146; compensation insurance carrier and various states to collateralize obligations for outstanding claims.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In estimating the fair value of derivative positions, SFN utilizes quoted market prices, if available, or quotes obtained from outside sources.&nbsp; As of December 26, 2010, SFN had one outstanding forward contract to sell CAD$6.2 million in January 2011.&nbsp; This derivative had a fair value or cost to unwind that is not material to SFN&#146;s consolidated results of operations.</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">10.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; EMPLOYEE SAVINGS AND INVESTMENT PLANS</FONT></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The SFN Group 401(k) Benefit Plan (the &#147;Plan&#148;) covers substantially all eligible employees of the controlled group, except employees working in Tatum.&nbsp; The Plan provides an employer match to certain eligible employees, which is based on employee contributions; however, the match was suspended as of April 2009.&nbsp; Employer contributions by SFN under the plan amounted to $0.2 million and $0.8 million for fiscal years 2009 and 2008, respectively.&nbsp; There were approximately 5,000 participating employees in the Plan as of December 26, 2010.</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; During the first quarter of 2010, SFN acquired Tatum, which also sponsored a 401(k), the Tatum Retirement Plan (the &#147;Tatum Plan&#148;). Employer contributions under the Tatum Plan amounted to $0.5 million for fiscal year 2010. There were approximately 775 participating employees in the Tatum Plan as of December 26, 2010.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN also has a voluntary non-qualified deferred compensation plan (the &#147;DCP&#148;) for highly compensated employees who are not fully eligible to participate in SFN&#146;s 401(k) Benefit Plan.&nbsp; The DCP is not formally funded, however, SFN maintained investments of $19.6 million and $17.4 million in a portfolio of mutual funds held in trust at December 26, 2010 and December 27, 2009, respectively.&nbsp; These balances are classified as &#147;Other current assets&#148; and &#147;Other assets&#148; in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets based on historical timing of distributions.&nbsp; Earnings or losses from these investments are intended to match earnings or losses in participant accounts.&nbsp; These investments could be used to satisfy general corporate purposes.&nbsp; The deferred compensation liability and accumulated investment earnings or losses are accrued.&nbsp; Such accrual amounted to $19.7 million and $17.6&nbsp;million at December 26, 2010 and December 27, 2009, respectively.&nbsp; The long-term deferred compensation liability is $17.6 million and the short-term portion of the liability of $2.1 million is within &#147;Other current liabilities&#148; in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets, classified based on historical timing of distributions.&nbsp; Employee deferrals within the DCP relating to SFN stock are included in treasury stock within the stockholders&#146; equity section of the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets (rather than in &#147;Other long-term liabilities&#148;) as employees may only be paid out in shares of SFN stock.&nbsp; There were approximately 160 employees participating in the DCP plan as of December 26, 2010.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">11.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES</FONT></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
<A name="CommandContin"></A>Substantially all of SFN&#146;s operations are conducted in leased premises.&nbsp; SFN also leases computers and other equipment.&nbsp; Total lease expense for the fiscal years ended 2010, 2009 and 2008 was $19.3&nbsp;million, $20.1 million and $25.8 million, respectively.&nbsp; Future minimum lease payments under non-cancelable leases as of December 26, 2010 are $20.0&nbsp;million, $16.0 million, $9.6&nbsp;million, $5.6&nbsp;million and $4.3 million in the years 2011 through 2015, respectively, and $7.7&nbsp;million thereafter which are partially offset by $0.5 million under future non-cancelable subleases.&nbsp; Of these future minimum lease payments, $1.5&nbsp;million has been accrued as of December 26, 2010, related to facility closures, which is included as part of &#147;Other current liabilities&#148; and &#147;Other long-term liabilities&#148; in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets.</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; SFN had outstanding irrevocable letters of credit of approximately $31.9&nbsp;million and surety bonds outstanding of approximately $0.2 million as of December 26, 2010.&nbsp; These instruments primarily collateralize SFN&#146;s recorded obligations under workers&#146; compensation insurance programs.&nbsp; The level of collateral required is determined by the insurance carrier based on claims experience of the programs and may vary from year to year.&nbsp; As of December 26, 2010, none of these irrevocable letters of credit had been drawn upon. </FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><B><FONT style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN GROUP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES</FONT></B></FONT></B></P>
<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><B><FONT style="mso-bidi-font-weight: normal"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS- (Continued)</FONT></B></FONT></B></P>
