<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">11.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES (Continued)</FONT></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><STRONG><FONT size=2></FONT></STRONG>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 35.3pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN, in the ordinary course of its business, is or may be threatened with or named as a defendant in various lawsuits.&nbsp; SFN maintains insurance in such amounts and with such coverages and deductibles as management believes are reasonable and prudent.&nbsp; The principal risks that SFN insures against are workers&#146; compensation, personal injury, bodily injury, property damage, professional malpractice, errors and omissions, and fidelity losses.&nbsp; SFN&#146;s management does not expect that the outcome of any pending lawsuits relating to such matters, individually or collectively, will have a material adverse effect on SFN&#146;s financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.</FONT>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 35.3pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 35.3pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">On December&nbsp;13, 2004, and as amended on January&nbsp;13, 2005 and October&nbsp;31, 2005, Glidepath Holding B.V. and Jeimon Holdings N.V., as plaintiffs, filed an action against SFN Group, Inc. in the U.S. District Court of the Southern District of New York.&nbsp; Glidepath and Jeimon Holdings, investors in the entity that acquired the Cyber Center business of Spherion Technology (UK) Limited, a subsidiary of SFN Group, Inc., in 2002, sued SFN for fraud, negligent misrepresentation, aiding and abetting, breach of fiduciary duty and unjust enrichment and seek $32.0 million in damages, and treble for punitive damages, plus attorneys&#146; fees, expert fees and costs.&nbsp; Glidepath and Jeimon Holdings allege that an individual who was an officer of Spherion Technology (UK) fraudulently induced them to invest in a corporation formed to purchase the Cyber Center business, while he remained in the employ of Spherion Technology (UK) and was to be paid an incentive bonus for the sale by SFN.&nbsp; They allege that he misled them as to his employment status at the time, as to the prospects for the Cyber Center, and as to whether the newly formed corporation was assuming the indebtedness of Spherion Technology (UK) associated with the Cyber Center business.&nbsp; They allege that in doing so, he was acting as SFN&#146;s agent.&nbsp; On November 14, 2008, based upon information obtained through discovery, SFN filed counterclaims against plaintiffs under theories of contract interference and unjust enrichment.&nbsp; SFN alleges that plaintiffs interfered with SFN&#146;s employment relationship with its Spherion Technology (UK) Limited officer, and recovered and retained damages in a U.K. arbitration proceeding against such officer, which damages belonged to SFN.&nbsp; Cross-motions for summary judgment were filed by the parties and fully briefed before the court on May 1, 2009.&nbsp; On March 30, 2010, the court granted SFN&#146;s motion for summary judgment in the action filed against SFN by plaintiffs Glidepath and Jeimon Holdings, and dismissed plaintiffs&#146; claims against SFN.&nbsp; The court also granted plaintiffs&#146; motion for summary judgment on the counterclaims asserted by SFN against the plaintiffs, and dismissed SFN&#146;s counterclaims against the plaintiffs.&nbsp; The plaintiffs have appealed the judgment granting SFN&#146;s motion for summary judgment, and SFN has cross-appealed the judgment granting the plaintiffs&#146; motion for summary judgment. The appeals have not yet been fully briefed, and a </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face=sans-serif><FONT face="Times New Roman">hearing date for oral arguments on the appeals has not been set at this time.</FONT> </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN intends to continue vigorously defending this matter and management believes the likelihood of a loss is remote.&nbsp; SFN accrued $0.4 million related to legal fees incurred to defend this matter and does not have insurance coverage for this claim.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 0.35in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The State of </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">California has assessed the Company $1.6 million plus potential interest and penalty of $1.3 million as a result of a dispute related to 2003 state unemployment tax rates.&nbsp; An appeals court in the State of California ruled against the Company on a procedural basis in 2010, and the Company expects to pay the assessment, intrest and penalty in 2011.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 26, 2010, the full amount of the assessment, including interest and penalty, was accrued in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets in &#147;Accounts payable and other accrued expenses&#148;.&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; On July 21, 2010, the Company received a grand jury subpoena from the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York for documents concerning its contracts for work on a timekeeping system project for the City of New York.&nbsp; In December 2010, two subcontractors to the Company were arrested and charged with fraud in connection with the U.S. Attorney's investigation.&nbsp; On January 13, 2011, the Company received an additional federal grand jury subpoena for documents related to the project.&nbsp; The Company is continuing to cooperate with the U.S. Attorney's investigation.&nbsp; The Company has not been informed that it is a target of any investigation.&nbsp; The Company has accrued $2.5 million related to this matter for receivables and contract exposures, as well as legal fees.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=center><FONT size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">12.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; STOCKHOLDERS&#146; EQUITY</FONT></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 35pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt">
<A name="StockEquity"></A><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">On February 17, 2009, the Board of Directors authorized the Company to repurchase up to an average of 50,000 per week on an annual basis of the Company&#146;s common stock primarily for the purpose of offsetting dilution created through the Company&#146;s various employee benefit plans.&nbsp; During the fiscal years 2010 and 2009, SFN purchased 0.5 million shares for approximately $4.9 million at an average price per share of $9.63, and 2.4 million shares for approximately $8.9 million at an average price per share of $3.72, respectively.</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">13.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; STOCKHOLDER RIGHTS PLAN</FONT></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><STRONG><FONT size=2></FONT></STRONG>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt">
<A name="StockholderRights"></A><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; On March&nbsp;17, 1994, SFN entered into a Rights Agreement </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">with the Bank of New York Mellon, as Rights Agent,</FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> to protect stockholders in the event of an unsolicited attempt to acquire SFN which is not believed by the Board of Directors to be in the best interest of stockholders.&nbsp; Under the Rights Agreement, a dividend of one right (a &#147;Right&#148;) per share was declared and paid on each share of SFN&#146;s common stock outstanding on April&nbsp;1, 1994.&nbsp; As to shares issued after such date, rights will automatically attach upon issuance.&nbsp; The Rights are scheduled to expire on April 1, 2014, unless extended by the Board of Directors.</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">On September 9, 2009, the Company entered into an amendment (the &#147;Seventh Amendment&#148;) to its Rights Agreement to reduce the threshold at which a person or group becomes an &#147;Acquiring Person&#148; from 15% to 4.9% and expanded the concept of ownership to include shares indirectly and constructively owned under the tax rules governing ownership changes.&nbsp; The purpose of this amendment was to help preserve the value of the net operating loss benefits and other deferred tax assets of SFN.&nbsp; The value of tax assets that the Company is protecting by this amendment is $137.0 million, as reflected on the Company&#146;s balance sheet as of December 26, 2010.&nbsp; The Company&#146;s ability to use its net operating losses (&#147;NOLs&#148;) and other tax benefits would be substantially limited by Section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the &#147;Code&#148;), if an &#147;ownership change&#148; occurred &#150; generally, a greater than 50 percentage point change in ownership of common stock by shareholders owning (or deemed to own under Section 382 of the Code) five percent or more of a corporation&#146;s stock over a defined period of time.&nbsp; The Company regularly monitors ownership changes (as calculated for purposes of Section 382) and, as of December 26, 2010, we were below the 50 percent ownership change level that would limit our ability to utilize our NOLs and other tax benefits.</FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; On May 10, 2010, the Company entered into another amendment to the Rights Agreement (the &#147;Eighth Amendment&#148;), to reduce the maximum term of the Seventh Amendment from April 1, 2014 to September 9, 2012.&nbsp; The Seventh Amendment may also expire at an earlier date upon the occurrence of certain events as set forth therein.&nbsp; The Company&#146;s stockholders approved the Seventh Amendment, as amended by the Eighth Amendment, at the Company&#146;s 2010 annual meeting.&nbsp; If the Seventh Amendment expires, the Rights Agreement will continue (without the provisions of the Seventh or Eighth Amendments) until the expiration of the Rights or their earlier redemption or exchange pursuant to the terms of the Rights Agreement. </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The Rights Agreement will be submitted to a vote of stockholders at the next annual meeting following the review of the Rights Agreement by the Three-year Independent Director Evaluation Committee of the Board in 2012, if at such time the Board of Directors determines it is appropriate to continue any provision of the Rights Agreement. If such stockholder approval is not obtained, then the Board of Directors will immediately terminate the Rights Agreement.</FONT></P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; TEXT-INDENT: 35pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Net loss for the fiscal year ended December 28, 2008, includes $3.4 million of pre-tax loss from operations related to legal fees associated with the defense of certain foreign legal matters.&nbsp; The Company recorded a pre-tax loss on disposal of $2.8 million to increase established reserves to an amount of $5.5 million to reflect the settlement of certain indemnification claims relating to the sale of the Australian education business in 2004.&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">15.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; RESTRUCTURING AND OTHER CHARGES</FONT></B></P>
<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 35pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">During 2010, SFN incurred $3.6 million for transaction and integration costs related to the acquisition of Tatum, offset by $0.3 million positive development from a prior year legal matter which is included in restructuring and other charges on the accompanying Condensed Consolidated Statement of Operations. In 2009, SFN incurred other charges of $5.4 million for lease and severance-related costs related to the elimination of underutilized staff and the consolidation of certain branch locations due to the contraction of the U.S. economy and the continued decline of revenues and gross profit and $1.7 million related primarily to adverse developments in a prior year legal matter.&nbsp; In 2008, $11.4 million was incurred related to severance and facility closures as a result of cost containment efforts including $1.9 million of severance, facility closure and project completion costs related to the integration of Technisource and Todays Staffing.</FONT></P>

<A name="SegmentInfo"></A></FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">SFN has two operating segments: Professional Services and Staffing Services.&nbsp; SFN evaluates the performance of its operating segments and allocates resources based on revenues, gross profit and segment operating profit.&nbsp; Segment operating profit is defined as income before unallocated corporate costs, goodwill and intangible asset impairment, amortization expense, interest expense, interest income, income taxes and restructuring and other charges.&nbsp; All intercompany revenues and expenses have been eliminated</FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">.&nbsp; </FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Additionally, amounts related to discontinued operations have been excluded from the segment information below and are presented as discontinued operations in the Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations.&nbsp; As a result of internal organizational and business strategy changes, SFN realigned its operating segments during the first quarter of 2010.The historical segment information has been adjusted to conform to SFN&#146;s segment presentation in 2010, moving the managed service program (&#147;MSP&#148;)and professional contingent workforce services operated under the SourceRight brand into Professional Services from Staffing Services. In addition, several large clerical customers previously reported as part of Professional Services are now managed and reported as part of Staffing Services.</FONT></P>
